domain_descriptions.activity: Production, enterprise conditions and physical throughput that bear on current activity.
domain_descriptions.firm_health: Sales, margins, financing conditions and enterprise-survey aggregates without respondent records.
domain_descriptions.investment: Capital formation, market flows, transport investment and property-linked expenditure.
domain_descriptions.credit: Money-market prices, bank credit, social financing and external-account aggregates.
domain_descriptions.inflation: Prices, housing indices, funding rates and independently observed currency references.
domain_descriptions.labor: Published employment and hiring aggregates; household and applicant microdata remain out of scope.
domain_descriptions.property: Official city indices and licensed aggregate substitutes, never parcel or household dossiers.
domain_descriptions.trade: Customs, settlement, port and currency evidence with explicit release clocks.
domain_descriptions.consumer_digital: Aggregate consumption, parcel, mobility and search-demand signals where lawful access exists.
domain_descriptions.commodities: Energy, industrial materials, atmospheric telemetry and trade-linked physical evidence.
domain_descriptions.agriculture: Published agricultural trade and production aggregates; no farm-level respondent collection.
domain_descriptions.logistics: Rail, port, parcel, mobility and transport throughput with source-specific cadence limits.

release_source_aliases.note: The release monitor and registry entry describe the same CFETS benchmark family.
The monitored NBS energy bulletin belongs to the NBS official-statistics family; it is not evidence that the planned National Data adapter is live.
The monitored industrial bulletin belongs to the NBS official-statistics family; it does not activate the planned National Data adapter.
The monitored National Railway Administration release has no matching source-registry entry. It remains explicit and is not joined to the distinct Ministry of Transport adapter target.
Both are PBOC statistical releases, but this monitor does not by itself make the credit/TSF adapter live.
Open-market-operation notices share a publisher with the credit/TSF family but are a different release surface.
The settlement monitor is one SAFE publication family; it does not imply every external-account series is collected.
